evidence_items.summary: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting drinking and agricultural water demands in India. This review focuses on regional variations in groundwater quality, contamination sources, and remediation strategies. The evaluation encompasses pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, hardness, major ions, and contaminants including fluoride, arsenic, nitrate, and heavy metals. Results reveal significant regional variations, with contamination driven by intensive agriculture, industrial activities, mining, urbanization, and geological factors. Water Quality Index assessments indicate that while many groundwater sources meet drinking standards, numerous sites exceed permissible limits, requiring treatment. Contamination stems from both natural processes (mineral dissolution and rock–water interactions) and anthropogenic activities (fertilizer application, industrial effluents, domestic sewage, and mining operations). Health risk assessments demonstrate elevated noncarcinogenic risks in fluoride- and nitrate-affected areas, causing fluorosis, arsenicosis, methemoglobinemia, and other waterborne diseases. Various remediation approaches suitable for Indian conditions have been investigated, including membrane-based systems, electrochemical methods, adsorption techniques, and nature-based solutions. This review provides an integrated understanding of India’s regional groundwater quality challenges and emphasizes the necessity for targeted interventions, enhanced monitoring, and sustainable management strategies to protect groundwater resources. The review further provides an integrated regional comparison framework linking contamination sources, hydrogeochemical processes, health risks, and remediation strategies for groundwater management in India.
evidence_items.title: Groundwater Contamination in India: Regional Variations, Hydrogeochemical Controls, Health Risks, and Integrated Management Strategies

organizations: Biology, Rivers State University, Port Harcourt, Rivers State,  Nigeria
evidence_items.summary: This study assessed the physicochemical parameters and heavy metal (Pb, Cd, Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn) concentrations in surface water of Mgbuodahia River, Niger Delta, Nigeria, for six months (May October 2025) across four stations (ST1–ST4). Physicochemical parameters were measured in situ, heavy metals were quantified by atomic absorption spectrophotometry, and data were evaluated using a General Linear Model ANOVA with Tukey’s pairwise comparison. Dissolved oxygen was low (0.62±0.12 mg/L) and biochemical oxygen demand elevated (8.41±4.20 mg/L), indicating organic pollution. Lead (0.33±0.10 mg/L) and cadmium (0.10±0.06 mg/L) exceeded WHO permissible limits (0.01 and 0.003 mg/L respectively) at every station and month. ANOVA showed significant monthly variation for pH, conductivity, temperature and most heavy metals, while chromium showed no significant station or month effect, suggesting a diffuse rather than point-source origin. Nickel showed a pronounced June peak roughly double every other month's mean, indicating an episodic input event. These concentrations are higher than values reported for several other Niger Delta water bodies, indicating that Mgbuodahia River is affected by lead and cadmium inputs. The study concludes that Mgbuodahia River is impacted by organic and heavy metal pollution and recommends continuous monitoring and regulation of discharge into the river.
evidence_items.title: Physicochemical Parameters and Heavy Metal Contamination of  Surface Water of Mgbuodahia River, Niger Delta, Nigeria

evidence_items.summary: Measuring welfare in the informal sector can be biased when it relies on fluctuating nominal income rather than actual household expenditure. This study applies the Capability Approach to examine how resources shape the economic functioning of informal worker households in Gunungkidul, Indonesia, using real household consumption expenditure as a proxy for functioning. The study contributes by shifting the unit of analysis to households and introducing the District Minimum Wage (UMK) as a conceptual benchmark. Using March 2025 National Socioeconomic Survey (Susenas) data covering 464 informal worker households, the study applies binary logistic regression. The model shows good discriminatory capacity, with an AUC of 0.788 and a Nagelkerke R-squared of 0.321. Male-headed households have substantially higher odds of achieving expenditure above the UMK. Financial inclusion shows contrasting effects: account ownership is negatively associated with the outcome, while credit, digital money, and combined financial services are positively associated, with combined services showing the largest odds ratio. Business-oriented internet use has a stronger positive association than general internet access. Higher education and longer working hours are positively associated with the probability of expenditure above the UMK, whereas age has a negative association. The findings highlight the importance of human capital, productive financial inclusion, business-oriented digitalization, and demographic characteristics in expanding the economic capabilities of informal worker households.
evidence_items.title: Determinants of Economic Functioning among Informal Worker Households Using the District Minimum Wage as a Benchmark: Empirical Evidence from Gunungkidul

evidence_items.summary: Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa {D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa {R} = 0.15\)). On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check. We report this figure and then show, using a format-controlled negative (N1) on the same 1,800 IDs, that it measures format asymmetry between source and response rather than hallucination detection. The tribunal flags 1,569 of 1,800 verbatim correct answers presented alone (87.2%), and in HaluEval-QA scores the correct answer as more anomalous than the hallucinated response. Three further findings follow from the same audit. (i) A per-module analysis shows the tribunal has no content-sensitive module in its current set: the one module designed to capture semantic divergence (cre isi) gives the same per-ID score whether the response is byte-identical or completely different. (ii) The 87.97-point advantage of multiplicative combination over weighted averaging reported in v4 is an artifact of threshold calibration; under per-scheme thresholds on format-matched negatives, both schemes converge to F1 \(\approx 0.69\) and the multiplicative scheme is worse by AUROC. (iii) Adding a semantic-equivalence guard makes the tribunal and a Jaccard baseline statistically indistinguishable (F1 0.720 vs. 0.722; AUROC 0.881 vs.
evidence_items.title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Ultrasonic communication through steel has emerged as a technically challenging but operationally transformative capability for subsea inspection and monitoring. This paper focuses on an ultrasonic system for transmitting high-rate data from a smart pig through steel barriers in a subsea environment, examining phased-array beamforming, array geometry, mounting strategies, signal design, and model- led performance evaluation. The work presented here reflects the current stage of the research, which remains simulation-driven but is now transitioning toward hardware prototyping and experimental validation. The paper presents a detailed analysis of 1D and 2D phased-array behaviour, including the influence of element spacing, aperture size, curvature, and mounting configuration on beam focus, energy delivery, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Analytical and numerical simulations, along with a fully parametric 3D model for finite element analysis (FEA), are used to refine the design and quantify the expected performance. The results demonstrate that phased-array beamforming can significantly improve energy delivery through steel, enabling high-bandwidth ultrasonic communication through metal barriers. The paper also examines the use of high-performance Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) encoding for ultrasonic communication, the implementation of row-column addressing for large arrays, and the integration of high-voltage drivers and low- noise receiver electronics. The paper underscores research maturity, technical depth, and the pragmatic considerations essential for transitioning from modelling to prototype development and concludes with a roadmap for this next research phase.
evidence_items.title: Directional Data: Ultrasonic Beamforming to Unlock Pipeline Inspection Data

evidence_items.summary: This study sought to evaluate the mycological contamination levels in both expired and non-expired dairy canned food products available at ADewaneyh Market. A total of 80 samples, consisting of 40 expired and 40 non-expired dairy canned products, were randomly collected from different retail outlets. Samples underwent mycological analysis employing standard microbiological methods, encompassing the isolation, identification, and quantification of fungal contaminants. The results showed that expired products had higher fungal counts and a wider range of species than non-expired products. The predominant fungi identified were Aspergillus spp., Penicillium spp., and Fusarium spp., with certain species acknowledged as potential mycotoxin producers. The presence of these fungi was linked to physical damage to packaging, bad storage conditions, and a longer shelf life. This study shows how eating expired dairy products could be bad for public health and stresses how important it is to store, handle, and regulate dairy canned food products properly to keep them from getting moldy.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Mycological Contamination in Expired and Non-Expired Dairy Canned Food Products Sold from Al-Dewaneyh Market

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS) is widely applied in heavy oil reservoirs to reduce oil viscosity and restore production through repeated steam injection, soak, and production cycles. In multilayer reservoirs, however, steam can preferentially enter shallow, depleted, watered-out, or higher-permeability intervals, resulting in poor steam conformance, excessive water production, and limited stimulation of deeper target zones. This paper presents a three-well field application where high-temperature thermal tubular patch technology was deployed to isolate shallow perforated intervals and redirect steam into deeper productive layers. The system comprises blank tubular sections with hydraulically expanded metal-to-metal sealing elements at both ends, providing a robust internal barrier capable of withstanding repeated high-temperature steam cycles. The workflow included production-history review, casing diagnostics, patch placement design, hydraulic expansion, post-installation verification, and production surveillance after CSS restart. The three pilot wells achieved peak oil-rate improvements of approximately 179%, 292%, and 242% compared with pre-intervention baselines, together with water-cut reductions from 97% to 88%, 98% to 90%, and 96% to 68%, respectively. The results confirm improved steam placement, successful shallow-zone isolation, and material production uplift. The intervention also demonstrated strong indicative economics, with a combined incremental oil rate of 482 BOPD and short payback sensitivity under reasonable netback assumptions. The work establishes a scalable intervention model for CSS well rejuvenation by applying a metal-to-metal thermal tubular patch to redirect steam into deeper target intervals.
evidence_items.title: Rejuvenating Steam Inflow Performance in Cyclic Steam Stimulation Wells Using Innovative Thermal Tubular Patch Technology: A New Benchmark for Heavy Oil Wells

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect content, a risk that is unacceptable when public institutions disclose scientific and legal information. This study presents and evaluates a hybrid agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that automates first-level responses to citizen information requests at the Marine Institute of Peru (IMARPE). A baseline analysis of 196 requests showed a mean response time of 12 business days, above the 10-day legal limit, and identified 26.9% of them as routine, data-extractable queries. The system, developed under CRISP-DM, uses LangGraph to route each query to a LightRAG knowledge graph (Neo4j) built from institutional yearbooks, to a Text-to-SQL agent that queries the IMARSIS relational database through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), or to both, with Gemini 2.5 Flash as the foundation model and a referral protocol for out-of-scope requests. Five institutional domain experts rated 30 test cases, with mean scores of 4.45/5 for factual accuracy, 4.10/5 for completeness, and 4.57/5 for clarity. Mean end-to-end software latency was 20.43 s (maximum 49.20 s), and 30 pilot users rated usability at 80.42 on the System Usability Scale (Cronbach’s α = 0.96). These preliminary, single-site results indicate that combining graph-based and SQL-based grounding is feasible for routine citizen-information services; comparison with simpler baselines remains pending.
evidence_items.title: A Hybrid Agentic RAG Architecture with Knowledge Graphs and Text-to-SQL for Automating Citizen Services in a Public Scientific Institution
ClinStigma: A Clinician-Guided Framework for Developing Synthetic Benchmarks of Contextual Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation

evidence_items.summary: Open-source uncensored large language models (ULLMs) are increasingly available in public LLM ecosystems. By removing or weakening safety guardrails, these models can comply with harmful requests, generate unsafe content, and be readily reused in downstream systems. While prior work has demonstrated the misuse potential of individual uncensored models, little has been done to systematically understand the ULLM ecosystem in real-world settings. In this paper, we present a systematic study of the open-source ULLM ecosystem. We analyzed 22,096 ULLMs collected from five major LLM hosting platforms and examined them across five interconnected components: artifacts, development, propagation, governance, and adoption. Our analysis shows that ULLMs are produced through four major methods, supported by a rich ecosystem of publicly available tools and uncensored datasets. We further found that ULLMs propagate widely across platforms, forming 4,457 cross-platform clusters comprising 11,094 models, with Hugging Face serving as the dominant upstream source. We uncovered systemic governance and security gaps, including inconsistent moderation labels applied to ULLMs across platforms, cross-platform propagation of ULLMs flagged with threat indicators, and frequent violations of base-model licensing constraints. ULLMs are also actively deployed in diverse real-world settings, including web applications, GitHub projects, underground forums, and model routing platforms, significantly lowering the barrier to harmful use. Our findings indicate that ULLMs are not isolated model artifacts but components of a broader ecosystem in which supply-chain dynamics, weak governance, and diverse downstream deployments jointly amplify risks.
evidence_items.title: Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral curiosity to a core feature of modern medical education through adaptive learning, simulation-based training, automated assessment, and large language models such as ChatGPT. Publication activity has accelerated rapidly, but the structure of this expanding literature has not been comprehensively mapped. Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy that combined medical education terms in the title field with artificial intelligence terms in the topic field. Articles, review articles, and data papers published from 2000 to 2026 were included. A total of 2,298 records were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analyses, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct keyword co-occurrence, country collaboration, and institutional collaboration networks. Data for 2026 represent a partial calendar year. Publication output remained limited until the late 2010s and rose sharply after 2021. Of the 2,298 records, 2,066 (89.9%) were published from 2021 to 2026, with the highest complete-year output in 2025 (821 publications). The United States led in publication volume (918 records) and raw citation count (14,582 citations), followed by the People’s Republic of China (367 records; 4,404 citations). The Journal of Surgical Education published the most articles. Harvard Medical School led institutional output, whereas Stanford University and the University of California San Francisco had higher raw citation totals despite fewer publications. Artificial intelligence, medical education, ChatGPT, medical students, and machine learning were the most prominent keywords. Artificial intelligence in medical education is a rapidly expanding but geographically and institutionally concentrated field. Raw citation patterns differed from publication volume, although these unadjusted measures should not be interpreted as direct comparisons of research quality. Thematic patterns emphasize learner-facing applications, assessment, and generative AI, while responsible curricular integration and empirical evaluation remain important priorities. These findings are especially relevant to emergency medicine education, where simulation, time-sensitive decision-making, and competency assessment are central.
evidence_items.title: Charting the rise of artificial intelligence in medical education: a global bibliometric and network analysis, 2000–2026

evidence_items.summary: Digital twin technology has emerged as a profound paradigm for bridging physical systems and their virtual counterparts through real-time data synchronization and interactive three-dimensional visualization. However, existing digital twin platforms are predominantly domain-specific, proprietary, and reliant on dedicated software infrastructure, severely limiting accessibility, interoperability, and cross-domain applicability. This paper presents a Universal Digital Twin (UDT) framework based on open web standards that incorporates AI as an architectural component alongside immersive XR interaction through a human-centered, bidirectional architecture. The proposed five-layer framework ensures real-time synchronization between physical and virtual systems while providing a foundation for AI-assisted decision-making and enabling users to influence system behavior through AR/VR interfaces. Implemented using Three.js and WebXR, the platform supports domain-agnostic applications, optimized 3D visualization, real-time telemetry monitoring, and intelligent analytics powered by large language models, physics-informed neural networks, and reinforcement learning, all accessible through standard web browsers without specialized software. The performance of the proposed framework was evaluated using browser-based performance metrics, including Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), and execution profiling under different network and processing conditions. Experimental results indicate that the framework achieves fast loading times, stable rendering performance, and efficient visualization across constrained and unconstrained environments.
evidence_items.title: Human-Centered Digital Twins: A Bidirectional WebXR-Based Architecture for Immersive Interaction
Comparative evaluation of lightweight CNN architectures for efficient and explainable deepfake detection

evidence_items.summary: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention but remains a high-demand psychomotor and cognitive procedure, characterized by operator dependency, variable performance, and substantial physical and mental workload. Increasing evidence links procedural quality and safety to clinician-related factors, including musculoskeletal strain, fatigue, and non-technical skills. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic technologies are emerging as potential tools to address these limitations. We conducted a scoping review with narrative synthesis of literature on human factors, ergonomics, AI, robotic technologies, and shared autonomy in colonoscopy and surgical robotics. Evidence synthesis: Colonoscopy performance remains limited by non-negligible miss rates and variability driven by both technical and human factors. Ergonomic constraints and cognitive workload contribute significantly to operator strain and may affect vigilance and decision-making. AI systems—including computer-aided detection (CADe), diagnosis (CADx), and quality monitoring—have demonstrated improvements in detection metrics and procedural standardisation, although concerns regarding cognitive offloading and potential deskilling persist. In parallel, emerging robotic and soft-robotic platforms aim to enhance navigation, improve procedural ergonomics, and reduce operator musculoskeletal strain, although clinical evidence remains limited. These technologies converge within a task-based shared-autonomy paradigm integrating physical, perceptual, and cognitive augmentation, with different procedural tasks operating at different levels of human–system control. A task-based shared-autonomy framework may provide a coherent model for integrating AI and robotics into colonoscopy while preserving human supervision and clinical judgement. Future developments should prioritise human-centred design, workflow integration, and multidimensional evaluation strategies to ensure safe and effective clinical implementation.
evidence_items.title: Augmenting colonoscopy with artificial intelligence and robotic assistance: a human-factors scoping review toward a task-based shared autonomy paradigm

evidence_items.summary: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the paradigm of instructional design. However, the micro-level process patterns of human-AI collaboration in generative AI-enabled instructional design for pre-service teachers still require in-depth analysis. This study aims to uncover the behavioral patterns and cognitive load characteristics of pre-service teachers when collaborating with generative AI to complete instructional design tasks and to explore the patterns of efficient human-AI collaboration. A total of 67 pre-service teachers completed instructional design tasks with AI assistance. A systematic instructional plan quality evaluation rubric was developed based on relevant theories, and participants were assigned to the high-quality and low-quality groups using a median split of their lesson-plan quality scores. The study employed lag sequential analysis to compare the behavioral sequence patterns between the two groups and measured their multidimensional cognitive load. The results indicate that the high-quality group exhibited a significant evaluation-revision bidirectional cycle and a revision self-loop, with a clear progressive sequence of “planning → decision-making → generation → evaluation → revision → re-evaluation” in their behavioral flow. In contrast, the low-quality group was mired in ineffective cycles, with fragmented behavioral logic. Key findings showed large effect sizes for the evaluation-revision cycle (r = 0.606) and for mental demand (r = 0.647). Regarding cognitive load, the high-quality group reported no greater subjective effort than the low-quality group (though this null finding should be interpreted with caution given the study’s power limitations). A second round of within-sample replication confirmed that these core findings were consistent across a second task. Based on the human-AI collaborative behavioral patterns and cognitive load of the high-quality and low-quality groups, the study constructed a model of the human-AI collaboration patterns in generative AI-enabled instructional design for pre-service teachers. Specifically, higher-quality outputs were associated with a pattern oriented toward cognitive efficiency, characterised by deep processing (evaluation-revision iteration) and by the avoidance of ineffective cycles. Conversely, lower-quality outputs co-occurred with ineffective cycles arising in the context of interaction obstacles, in which repeated clarifications and interrupted revisions were accompanied by higher cognitive and emotional load, describing a pattern of high investment with low output. Because participants were grouped on the basis of their design outcomes, these findings are correlational and do not establish the direction of the relationships; they nonetheless provide empirical evidence to inform the optimisation of human-AI collaboration in GenAI-supported instructional design.
evidence_items.title: Human–AI collaborative patterns in GenAI-supported instructional design among pre-service teachers: an analysis of interaction sequences and cognitive load

evidence_items.summary: Mammography is a key imaging modality for early breast cancer detection, but it involves exposure to ionizing radiation. This study aimed to establish local Diagnostic Reference Levels (LDRLs) for 2D and 3D mammography within Emirates Health Services (EHS) facilities to optimize radiation doses and enhance patient safety. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted across nine EHS facilities from February 2023 to June 2025. Data from 1184 women undergoing screening and diagnostic mammography were analyzed. Standard craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) projections were acquired using full-field digital mammography (2D, FFDM) and digital breast tomosynthesis (3D, DBT) systems with automatic exposure control (AEC). Only examinations with a compressed breast thickness (CBT) of 5.0 ± 0.5 cm were included to standardize radiation dose assessment. Extracted parameters included patient age, tube voltage (kVp), tube current–time product (mAs) and mean glandular dose (MGD). Local DRLs were defined as the 75th percentile of the MGD distribution for each projection and modality. For 2D mammography, mean ± standard deviation MGD values were 1.05 ± 0.51 mGy (CC) and 1.15 ± 0.57 mGy (MLO). For 3D mammography, mean ± standard deviation MGD values were higher at 1.87 ± 0.44 mGy (CC) and 2.08 ± 0.37 mGy (MLO). The resulting local DRLs were 1.30 mGy for CC and 1.46 mGy for MLO. EHS facility-level analysis indicated uniform dose distribution across all sites. The observed differences between 2D and 3D mammography doses reflect the inherently higher radiation requirements of tomosynthesis for volumetric imaging, consistent with international literature. Uniform distribution across EHS facilities suggests standardized protocols and effective quality control measures. The established LDRLs provide a practical tool for dose optimization, enabling radiology teams to benchmark their practices and identify potential areas for dose reduction without compromising image quality. Moreover, these findings support the development of a UAE national mammography dose registry, promoting patient safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous monitoring of radiation exposure trends. The study establishes local DRLs for mammography within EHS facilities, confirming that current practices are optimized for patient radiation safety while maintaining diagnostic quality. These LDRLs provide benchmarks for national dose optimization, support regulatory oversight, and form the foundation for a comprehensive UAE national mammography dose registry. Local Diagnostic Reference Levels (LDRLs) for mammography were established using data from nine Emirates Health Services facilities across the UAE. Mean glandular dose (MGD) values for both 2D full-field digital mammography and 3D digital breast tomosynthesis were within internationally accepted ranges. The derived LDRLs (1.30 mGy for CC and 1.46 mGy for MLO) indicate optimized radiation practices across participating facilities. The findings provide baseline evidence to support national dose optimization strategies and the future development of UAE mammography DRLs. Local Diagnostic Reference Levels (LDRLs) for mammography were established using data from nine Emirates Health Services facilities across the UAE. Mean glandular dose (MGD) values for both 2D full-field digital mammography and 3D digital breast tomosynthesis were within internationally accepted ranges. The derived LDRLs (1.30 mGy for CC and 1.46 mGy for MLO) indicate optimized radiation practices across participating facilities. The findings provide baseline evidence to support national dose optimization strategies and the future development of UAE mammography DRLs.
evidence_items.title: Establishment of local diagnostic reference levels for mammography: optimizing patient radiation dose within Emirates Health Services

evidence_items.summary: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.
evidence_items.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis

evidence_items.summary: The Internet of Agents (IoA) is emerging as a paradigm in which AI agents communicate and collaborate across organizational boundaries, attracting growing attention from both industry and standards communities. However, designing an agent communication protocol that can be deployed at both Internet and intranet scales remains an open challenge. In this paper, we present ATP (Agent Transfer Protocol), a server-mediated agent-to-agent communication protocol to address this agent interoperability challenge. ATP assigns each agent a local@domain identifier, discovers domain servers through DNS SVCB records, authenticates every cross-domain message with ATS sender policies and ATK signatures, and carries asynchronous messages, request/response calls, and event streams in one opaque envelope. We implement a Go-based ATP prototype and evaluate its practicality: the cross-domain authentication pipeline adds 0.60 ms median overhead, while stable-state throughput reaches 16.1 K messages/s within a domain and 5.5 K messages/s for cross-domain delivery at 128 connections.
evidence_items.title: Poster: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Authentication and Messaging for Agent-to-Agent Communication

evidence_items.summary:
Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global health challenge requiring exploration of alternative antimicrobial agents. Honey has documented antibacterial properties, but activity varies by composition, and data on locally available honeys against drug-resistant pathogens remain limited.
Aim: To compare the in vitro antibacterial activity of selected processed and unprocessed honeys against reference and drug-resistant bacterial isolates.
Setting: The study was conducted in Limpopo province, South Africa, using locally sourced honey products.
Methods: A laboratory-based experimental study evaluated four honeys, two unprocessed (A, B) and two processed (C, D), against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Streptococcus pyogenes and selected drug-resistant isolates, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli, carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined by broth microdilution, with disk diffusion used as a supplementary qualitative method. Data were analysed descriptively.
Results: Minimum inhibitory concentrations ranged from 3.13% to 25% volume/volume. Unprocessed B and Processed D showed lower MICs against several organisms. No inhibition zones were observed for reference P. aeruginosa or S. pyogenes. Processed D produced the largest inhibition zone against MRSA (8 mm). Higher MICs were observed for A. baumannii across the honey samples.
Conclusion: Selected honeys demonstrated variable in vitro antibacterial activity against reference and drug-resistant isolates. However, the absence of appropriate controls and compositional characterisation limits mechanistic and clinical interpretation.
Contribution: This exploratory study provides preliminary data on the antibacterial activity of locally available honeys and supports further investigation using appropriate controls, chemical profiling and clinically relevant models.
evidence_items.title: Exploratory comparative screening of antibacterial activity of processed and unprocessed honeys against wild-type and drug-resistant bacterial strains

evidence_items.summary: Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains. In this study, we therefore ask: how far can reasoning supervision be compressed without sacrificing capability? To this end, we propose an uncertainty-guided progressive contraction framework that concentrates supervision and optimization on the reasoning trajectories most valuable for learning. Specifically, rather than treating a teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) as a single realized path, we construct uncertainty-profiled reasoning supervision by building Monte Carlo reasoning trees around intermediate reasoning states to expose process-level uncertainty. This uncertainty first contracts the original corpus into a compact teacher-informed pool. A second, learner-aware contraction then performs online routing during SFT, concentrating optimization according to the student's evolving learning state. Together, the two stages progressively contract both supervision and optimization, substantially reducing the student training budget. Experiments across diverse reasoning benchmarks and LLM families show that our method uses as little as 0.22% of the optimization budget of full-data SFT, over 450x less training exposure, while maintaining or improving reasoning performance. Notably, our framework generalizes well across heterogeneous student families, black-box teachers, and weak-to-strong transfer. This indicates that it is not only a way to accelerate training but can also enhance reasoning capability.
evidence_items.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training

authors: The International Digital Twin Consortium in Healthcare
evidence_items.summary: Large language model (LLM) assistants are being deployed to clinicians across health systems, and judgments about their readiness rest largely on benchmark scores, most of them derived from examination questions or curated cases. A benchmark predicts performance in deployment only to the extent that its items resemble real use, yet whether benchmarks reflect the work these systems receive has rarely been measured. Here we analyze 127,833 queries sent by 6,342 physicians, advanced practice providers and nurses in 35 specialties to an institutional assistant during an eight-month roll-out. We characterize each query with RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework grounded in taxonomies of clinical questions and of LLM evaluation, which records its task, intent, answerability, missing information and potential harm. Documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use, and diagnosis 3.7%; more than a third of queries could not be answered well as posed. Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public benchmarks drawn from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports, which we assemble into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas, showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across task categories would. Benchmarks in suites designed to resemble clinical practice were individually no closer to real use than those used in frontier model reports. Benchmark scores therefore say little about how clinical AI performs on most of the work it is actually given, and evaluation should be matched to real clinical use.
evidence_items.title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated

evidence_items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet synthesizing diverse and reliable software environments at scale remains challenging. Native application environments require substantial construction and integration effort, which limits application coverage and increases the risk of application-specific overfitting. Browser-hosted environments provide limited interaction depth and workflow complexity. These limitations motivate SoftwareGym, an automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI software environments with diverse interfaces, executable functionality, and runtime-verified behavior. It generates structurally diverse designs, realizes them as runnable applications, and uses GUI evaluation with iterative repair to ensure functional reliability. Using SoftwareGym, we synthesize 182 applications across twelve categories and achieve a mean GUI task pass rate of 91.5%. We construct SoftwareGym-Bench, a 120-task evaluation suite spanning the same twelve categories, and use trajectories collected from these environments for CUA training. The resulting model improves Pass@3 from 41.39% to 56.97% on the strictly out-of-domain OSWorld benchmark and achieves 40.0% on SoftwareGym-Bench. These results demonstrate the potential of synthesized software environments as scalable and transferable supervision for CUA training.
evidence_items.title: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
